title: Executor Accord and Root Edit Primitives cannot be deactivated, so an Agent must wind down via the Termination Protocol
content:
A.2.2.1.2.4.2 grants Prime Agents general freedom to deactivate Primitives through their own Root Edit governance process, then A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1 and its children carve out the exceptions. A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1.2 gives the sharpest reasoning: Agents "must have active Executor Accord and Root Edit Primitives at all times," and once Globally Activated these "cannot be deactivated, as doing so renders the Agent unable to operate or make further changes to its Artifact." An Agent seeking to wind down must instead follow the termination process at A.1.14.5.

The justification is a **self-bricking argument**. The Root Edit Primitive is the Agent's amendment mechanism; deactivating it would destroy the only route by which the deactivation could ever be undone. This is an irreversible action whose irreversibility is not obvious to the actor taking it, so the Atlas removes the capability rather than relying on Agents to notice.

The companion prohibitions round out the set: Agent Creation, Transformation, and Agent Token Primitives (A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1.1) are single-deployment Primitives whose Global Status becomes `Completed` and immutable, and the Upkeep Rebate and Ecosystem Upkeep Fee Primitives (A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1.3, A.2.2.1.2.4.2.1.4) can never be deactivated at all.

The general principle: exit must be a *defined process*, not a side effect of turning things off. Redirecting wind-down to a named protocol keeps termination observable and orderly, where deactivation-as-exit would leave a silently inert Agent still nominally holding ecosystem status.
description: Deactivating either would leave an Agent unable to operate or amend its own Artifact — a bricked state — so the Atlas removes the option instead of warning against it.
